cases.title: A paid comparison without its method
cases.text: Constructed sponsored post: “These headphones last twice as long.” The post names no comparison model or test settings. What is the useful next check?
choices: Treat the claim as false because the creator was paid.
Find the comparison models, test conditions and relevant independent results.
Accept the claim because the post says sponsored.
cases.why: The comparison lacks a stated baseline and test conditions. Identify which models and settings were compared; a payment label alone cannot answer that measurement question.

cases.title: A selected customer quotation
cases.text: A constructed product page highlights one customer saying “Best value anywhere.” No price comparison or selection method is supplied. What should you check?
choices: Treat one enthusiastic quotation as a representative price comparison.
Decide whether the customer is genuine from the writing style alone.
Check value criteria, comparable prices and how the quoted accounts were selected.
cases.why: “Best value” needs criteria: price, included features and what was compared. One selected quotation does not supply those measurements or a defined sample.
